historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs on the net-revenue KPI (FY2022 4,337.6 / FY2020 3,213.8 -> FY2025 6,026); gross CSV revenue gives 11.6% / 14.6%. EPS FY2022 8.14 / FY2020 5.89 -> FY2025 10.90. Equity FY2022 8,471.8 / FY2020 6,168.3 -> FY2025 11,312. FCF on the owner basis (OCF ex-CCP - capex - SBC; lease principal ~EUR90-95m/yr is a near-constant level shift and barely moves the CAGR): FY2022 ~1,770 / FY2020 ~1,280 -> FY2025 2,247. History is flattered by M&A (Qontigo/ISS 2020-21, SimCorp 2023) and by the 2022-24 rate cycle lifting the treasury result from ~zero to ~EUR1bn; the organic ex-treasury run-rate is closer to the 8% the company targets to 2028. Equity CAGR selected (5yr 12.9% is acquisition-inflated). FCF CAGR below revenue CAGR because FY2020 cash flow was a COVID-volatility peak.

scenario_narratives.base: Plan-minus: organic ex-treasury growth slightly below the 8% target, treasury result flat around EUR0.8bn, margin creeps 1pp above the long-run 57-58% band. Value is driven by secular European capital-market deepening (custody, fund services, index) offset by trading cyclicality.
scenario_narratives.bull: Plan-plus: EMIR 3.0 clearing share gains at Eurex, double-digit custody/fund AUC growth from European retail and pension flows, SimCorp SaaS migration, and a rising treasury result in a higher-rate regime; operating leverage finally reaches the reported margin (~63%).
scenario_narratives.bear: 2026 proves the peak: rates and volatility both fall back in 2027, compressing the treasury result and transaction fees at once; LCH keeps the swap pool; ISS legal/regulatory costs and M&A integration weigh; margin reverts to ~57% and growth to 2.5-3.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Deutsche Börse is valued as a fee-based market-infrastructure operator on attributable owner FCF, standalone (pre-Allfunds), with CCP/banking balances kept out of both flows and net debt. The key judgment calls are (1) how much of 2026's strength is cyclical (treasury result + rates volatility), (2) whether the flat 57-58% margin history or management's operating-leverage story governs the outer years, and (3) excluding banking-book commercial paper from corporate net debt.
key_risks_to_valuation: Treasury result (~12% of net revenue) is a direct function of ECB rates and customer cash balances; a cutting cycle removes it at near-100% margin
Trading/clearing volumes are cyclical; FY2026 is boosted by a geopolitical energy shock and rate volatility
Allfunds (~EUR5.3bn, 70% cash) adds leverage and share issuance; not in the standalone valuation
Clearstream Banking holds ~USD1.7bn of Bank Markazi client assets subject to a pending US turnover order (Peterson II) and EU sanctions treatment -- legal/sanctions tail risk
ISS proxy-advisory US regulatory exposure (SEC subpoena, state attorney-general suits)
Net debt basis: including EUR1.9bn commercial paper would lower IV ~EUR10.7/share

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular Xetra close); 52-week range 200.1-317.2
data_sources.financials: DB1.DE_Metrics.csv / core_metrics and kpis (NetRevenue); FY2025 annual report (staff-cost note for SBC, bond table, financial liabilities note, cash-flow statement); H1 2026 half-yearly report (balance sheet, note 6 bonds/CP/leases, note 11 EPS share counts, cash-flow statement); Q3 2026 quarterly statement (2026 guidance raise, hybrid/convertible issuance, bond redemption, NCI, segment data)
data_sources.qualitative: DB1.DE_Analysis.json (growth drivers, risks, bull/bear cases); FY2025 annual report 'Leading the Transformation' 2028 targets

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 180,287,660 shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 (H1 2026 note 11, after completion of the EUR500m buyback on 2026-06-26) + 183,950 potentially dilutive shares from share-based payment programmes = 180.47m. Q3 2026 basic average 180.2m confirms. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The EUR600m 0.5% convertible (Sept 2026, due 2031) is carried as debt at notional, not as dilution -- charged once. The Allfunds consideration (30% in DB1 shares) is NOT modelled: the deal is unclosed and the valuation is standalone.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, staff-cost note: 'Expenses from share-based payment' EUR45m (FY2024 EUR74.3m, FY2023 EUR60.1m, FY2022 EUR48.5m). Predominantly cash-settled (phantom LSI/RSU/performance shares) and already inside staff costs and reported EBITDA; no separate equity-award withholding-tax line. The financial-parser's SBC column is empty (candidates were bonus/pension provisions), so this was read directly from the filing. Forward charge 1.0% of net revenue (4-yr average ~1.1%; 2026 elevated by share-price performance per Q3 2026 statement).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:21Z Xetra regular close (Friday; valuation on Sunday 2026-10-25)
inputs.revenue_basis: base_revenue and all growth/margin paths are on the company's NET REVENUE KPI (sales revenue + treasury result + other operating income, LESS volume-related costs) -- EUR6,026m FY2025 -- not the CSV 'Revenue' column (EUR7,415m, which is gross of pass-through volume-related costs). EBITDA margins are therefore EBITDA / net revenue, the basis the company guides on (FY2026: net revenue >EUR6.5bn, EBITDA ~EUR3.9bn). Treasury result (~EUR0.8bn guided 2026) is interest earned on CUSTOMER cash balances at Clearstream/Eurex -- operating revenue, not interest on corporate net cash -- so it stays in the flows and nothing is stripped under the interest-income rule (DB1 is net-debt anyway).
inputs.net_debt_basis: Corporate debt only, CCP and banking-business balances excluded. Bonds issued (book) EUR6,735m at 2026-06-30 (H1 2026 note 6), adjusted for the disclosed Q3 2026 events: +EUR600m subordinated hybrid (4.2%, first call 2032; counted 100% as debt, no rating-agency equity credit), +EUR600m convertible (notional), -EUR1,000m 2023 bond redeemed 2026-09-28 => bonds EUR6,935m; + lease liabilities EUR523m (treatment A) = total_debt EUR7,458m. Cash = 'other cash and bank balances' EUR1,747m at 2026-06-30 + the EUR200m net Q3 issuance proceeds = EUR1,947m. Restricted bank balances (EUR64bn) and CCP instruments are member money and excluded. Commercial paper (EUR1,932m at H1 2026, up from EUR996m) is EXCLUDED: it funds Clearstream's banking book (H1 2026 'net increase in current receivables and securities from banking business >3 months' EUR702m moved with it) whose income sits in the treasury result -- matching-asset rule. The rating-relevant net debt (FY2025 EUR4,288m, nets 50% of hybrids and excess liquidity) is lower; including CP would cut IV by ~EUR10.7/share. Q3 2026 operating cash generation (~EUR0.6bn) is not credited because no Sep-30 debt/cash split is published -- conservative by ~EUR3/share.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities EUR523m (2026-06-30) in total_debt; lease principal (EUR90m FY2025) is NOT deducted from EBITDA, instead ROU renewal is charged through capex_pct_path (cash capex ~6.3-6.6% of net revenue + ~1.4% lease renewal = 7.8%). Tax EBIT uses total D&A including ROU depreciation, which is consistent under (A).
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: NCI profit (9M 2026 EUR76m = 4.2% of net profit, still ~EUR25m/quarter after the March 2026 buy-in of GA's 19.69% of ISS STOXX) is folded into cash_tax_rate_path as leakage: 1 - (1 - 27% effective tax)(1 - 4.2%) = 30%. NCI book (EUR402m at 2026-09-30) is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge. Calibration: FY2026E NOPAT at 30% ~EUR2.37bn vs attributable net profit run-rate ~EUR2.27bn + after-tax net financial expense ~EUR0.12bn = ~EUR2.40bn.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-built: 10y Bund ~3.0% (yields rose after the Sept 2026 ECB hike per Q3 statement) + beta 0.9 (Blume-adjusted exchange beta ~0.75, rounded up for the pending EUR5.3bn 70%-cash Allfunds deal raising leverage) x ERP 5.5% = CoE ~8.0%; after-tax cost of debt ~2.8% at ~9% D/(D+E) (net debt EUR5.5bn vs market cap ~EUR57bn) => WACC ~7.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; risk lives in the scenario flows (charged once).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with non-US adaptations (EUR WACC, lease treatment A, NCI folded into leakage). Routing: Deutsche Börse is an operating company (exchange, CCP, CSD/custody, fund services, software/data via SimCorp and ISS STOXX). It is NOT routed to the bank residual-income model despite Clearstream Banking and Eurex Clearing holding banking licences: the EUR400bn balance sheet is pass-through CCP margin, member deposits and settlement balances, earning a fee/treasury spread that is captured in net revenue; group earnings are fee-driven (~87% of 2026 net revenue ex-treasury) and capital needs are covered by retained earnings, not deposit growth. CCP and banking-business balances are excluded from net debt (see net_debt_basis); operating cash flow excludes CCP positions. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry). Buybacks: active repurchaser (EUR504m FY2025, EUR462m H1 2026), so the flat count is funded. PENDING ALLFUNDS ACQUISITION (binding Jan 2026, ~EUR5.3bn, 70% cash / 30% DB1 shares, close expected H1 2027, merger clearance pending): excluded from the flows, the debt and the share count -- this is a standalone valuation; the deal's per-share effect depends on synergy delivery and is a risk/upside around the scenarios, not inside them. FY0 = FY2025; year 1 = FY2026, ~75% reported already (9M 2026 net revenue EUR4,888m, EBITDA EUR2,964m) and guided to net revenue >EUR6.5bn / EBITDA ~EUR3.9bn.

bear.narrative: 2026 is a cyclical peak: the Middle-East energy shock and the Sept 2026 rate hikes drove interest-rate derivatives +48% and lifted the treasury result. In 2027 volatility normalises and the ECB reverses, so the treasury result falls back towards EUR0.5-0.6bn and transaction revenue stalls (net revenue +1%). LCH SwapClear keeps the euro swap pool despite EMIR 3.0, ISS faces US regulatory/legal costs (SEC subpoena, state suits), and integration of SimCorp/ISS STOXX/Allfunds absorbs management. Reported EBITDA margin reverts to the 2019-2025 norm of ~57%; growth settles at 2.5-3.5%.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands on guidance (net revenue ~EUR6.57bn, reported EBITDA ~59.5%). Organic ex-treasury growth runs a touch below the 8% 'Leading the Transformation' target while the treasury result holds ~flat near EUR0.8bn, so total net revenue grows 5-5.5% to 2028 and fades to 3%. Reported (post-SBC) EBITDA margin edges from 59.5% to 60.5% -- the 2019-2025 record is a remarkably flat 57-58% because acquisitions absorbed the operating leverage, so management's implied 61-62% by 2028 is not assumed.

bull.narrative: The 2028 plan is delivered in full and extended: European savings flow into funds/ETFs keeps custody and fund-processing AUC compounding at double digits, EMIR 3.0's active-account requirement moves a meaningful slice of euro swap clearing from LCH to Eurex, SimCorp One SaaS migration lifts IMS growth, and the treasury result grows with the renewed ECB hiking cycle. Costs held to ~3% growth push reported EBITDA margin to ~63% (management's 2028 implied 61-62% and beyond).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the FY2026 base year is cyclically elevated on two correlated axes (treasury result and interest-rate derivative volumes both ride the 2026 rate/volatility shock), so a simultaneous reversal is a single-event risk rather than two independent ones. Base 50%: the plan-minus path matches DB1's 15-year record of high-single-digit growth at a flat margin. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right (EMIR share gain vs a bank-owned LCH, margin breaking out of a seven-year 57-58% band, and treasury income rising further).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
